svg.title: SY20757 typical application
svg.desc: Typical application of the SY20757 power bank regulator, redrawn from the datasheet. The micro-USB input port connects VBUS to the IN pin, which has a 10 µF capacitor, and its D+ and D- lines to DPB and DMB. Two USB Type-A output ports, A1 and A2, take VBUS from the BUS net, which has a ≥ 20 µF capacitor, and their D+ and D- lines go to DPA and DMA pins. Each port's ground pin returns through a 10 mΩ sense resistor (RS1, RS2), with the SRP and SRN pins on either side of it, to an N-channel MOSFET (Q1, Q2) driven from the GA1/ITERM or GA2/VOCOM pin. A resistor and a diode, with no designator or value in the datasheet, sit across each MOSFET. RITERM on GA1/ITERM and RO_COMP on GA2/VOCOM are resistors to ground. LX drives a 2.2 µH inductor to the battery, with a 0.1 µF bootstrap capacitor from BST to LX and a ≥ 20 µF capacitor on the battery. BAT connects to the inductor's battery end. A 3.3 V regulator output VDD has a 1 µF capacitor and feeds the NTC divider, RNTC_UP (10 kΩ) above the thermistor RNTC (10 kΩ, 103-AT). The CV pin is left open, pulled low or pulled high to choose the charge voltage. RF from BAT to the KEY/FSW pin sets the boost frequency, and a key switch pulls the pin to ground. RCHG sets the charge current, RPEAK1 and RPEAK2 set the boost peak current and the battery resistance compensation, and four LEDs on LED1 to LED4 each have a resistor, RLED1 to RLED4, in parallel.
